analysis: Examined three changes. (1) EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift head 38-41 adds exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged allowlist. This is an exact-match selection; explicit contiguous/paged selections, the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV kill switch, VLM span-mask veto (base 88-96), crash-loop guard and degradesPagedFailure semantics are unchanged. Auto-selected paged failures may degrade to contiguous; this is existing policy. It raises default serving width to legacyMaximumConcurrency on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra (docs head 2344-2347), which affects availability/memory admission (TB-007, T-029-style DoS), but docs state native memory admission still bounds work (head 2359); no evidence of bypass. Prefix-cache posture (T-041) is not changed by backend selection in visible source; Flint docs say KV/checkpoint native only. (2) docs/architecture/inference.md head 2336-2348 documents constrained chaining: step N+1 sampled speculatively with mask of state N-1 and redrawn when state changes, plus maskCacheKey reuse. Security-relevant claim: tokens identical to unchained decode, so Flint protocol constraint (reasoning/call channel masking, EOS masking, answer-stop withholding) is preserved. Implementation lives in the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump f77b384c->fbd2cd0d, whose source was not supplied; correctness of redraw (that a token violating the state-N mask can never be emitted, and maskCacheKey fully captures allowed-set dependence, e.g. remaining budget, parallel_tool_calls, answer-stop match state) is unverified. A mis-keyed mask cache could leak withheld reasoning or bypass stop/tool framing (A-001 output integrity, T-007-adjacent), but that is a hypothesis without source. Integration should inspect the submodule's CBv2 constrained chaining and provider FlintNativeProtocolConstraint/FlintAnswerStopConstraint maskCacheKey implementations. No concrete regression identified from supplied evidence.
